paper.title_en: Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters. The resulting analytical hierarchy allows us to distinguish the interplay between both kinds of qubit-qubit interactions and the effects of displacement, neighboring-manifold mixing, and squeezing on the low-energy properties. We find that the transverse interaction mainly changes the collective-spin structure of the states, while the longitudinal interaction also modifies the displacement-dependent oscillator overlaps and introduces an additional two-boson coupling. We compare the analytical results with numerically exact diagonalization for the low-energy spectrum, ground-state energy, mean photon number, two-qubit concurrence, and spin correlations. The results provide a compact analytical description of how direct qubit-qubit interactions modify both the spectrum and the eigenstate structure beyond the rotating-wave approximation for few-qubit light-matter systems.
